source: Original (authored October 2026, no calculator). Laws of exponents: product, quotient, power of a power, power of a product, zero, negative and fractional exponents.

parts.label: a
parts.notes: A1 for 3^6 or 729. A bare answer earns the mark. 3^8 (multiplying exponents) or 9^6 (multiplying bases) earns A0.

parts.label: b
parts.notes: A1 for x^4. A bare answer earns the mark.

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept a^6 only. a^5 earns A0.
parts.notes: A1 for a^6. A bare answer earns the mark.

parts.label: d
parts.notes: A1 for the coefficient 4 (the 2 squared). A1 for x^6. The marks are independent: 2x^6 earns A0A1; 4x^5 earns A1A0. A bare answer earns both marks.

parts.label: e
parts.notes: A1 for the coefficient 3. A1 for x^3. The marks are independent. A bare answer earns both marks.

parts.label: f
parts.notes: A1 for 1. A bare answer earns the mark.

parts.label: g
parts.notes: A1 for 1/8. A bare answer earns the mark.

parts.label: h
parts.notes: A1 for 3. A bare answer earns the mark.

parts.label: i
parts.notes: M1 for any correct interpretation of the fractional exponent: (cube root of 8)^2, 2^2, or cube root of 64. A1 for 4. A correct value with no working earns A1 only (M0A1, house exception, markscheme-spec.md section 22).

parts.label: j
parts.notes: M1 for any correct handling of the negative fractional exponent: 1/4^(1/2), 1/sqrt(4), or (1/4)^(1/2). A1 for 1/2. A correct value with no working earns A1 only (M0A1).

source: Original (authored October 2026, no calculator). Simplifying radicals, like radicals, rationalizing a sqrt denominator, conjugate product, rationalizing with the conjugate. Radicals are prior learning; tagged 1.7 (rational exponents).

parts.label: a
parts.description: Simplify sqrt(12) in the form a sqrt(b).
parts.tolerance: Accept 2 sqrt(3) only. A decimal (3.46) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for writing 12 as a perfect square times another factor (sqrt(4) sqrt(3), or sqrt(4 x 3)). A1 for 2 sqrt(3). A correct answer with no working earns A1 only (M0A1).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Simplify sqrt(50) in the form a sqrt(b).
parts.notes: M1 for writing 50 as a perfect square times another factor (sqrt(25) sqrt(2)). A1 for 5 sqrt(2). A correct answer with no working earns A1 only (M0A1).

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept 4 or sqrt(16) simplified to 4. sqrt(16) left unsimplified earns A0.
parts.notes: A1 for 4. A bare answer earns the mark.

parts.label: d
parts.tolerance: Accept 7 sqrt(5) only. 7 sqrt(10) earns A0.
parts.notes: A1 for 7 sqrt(5). A bare answer earns the mark.

parts.label: e
parts.tolerance: Accept 2 sqrt(2) only. sqrt(16) = 4 earns M0A0.
parts.notes: M1 for rewriting sqrt(18) as 3 sqrt(2) (or otherwise expressing both terms as multiples of sqrt(2)). A1 for 2 sqrt(2). A correct answer with no working earns A1 only (M0A1).

parts.label: f
parts.notes: M1 for multiplying numerator and denominator by sqrt(3). A1 for 2 sqrt(3) or 6 sqrt(3)/3. A correct answer with no working earns A1 only (M0A1).

parts.label: g
parts.notes: M1 for a correct expansion with four terms (9 + 3 sqrt(5) - 3 sqrt(5) - 5) or the difference of two squares 3^2 - (sqrt(5))^2. A1 for 4. A correct answer with no working earns A1 only (M0A1).

parts.label: h
parts.description: Hence, rationalize the denominator of 8 / (3 - sqrt(5)).
parts.tolerance: Accept 6 + 2 sqrt(5) or 2(3 + sqrt(5)). Accept 8(3 + sqrt(5))/4 for the first A1 only.
parts.notes: M1 for multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate 3 + sqrt(5). A1 for the denominator 4 (any correct form of the new fraction, e.g. 8(3 + sqrt(5))/4). A1 for the simplified answer 6 + 2 sqrt(5) or 2(3 + sqrt(5)). Multiplying by 3 - sqrt(5) or by sqrt(5) earns M0.
parts.follow_through: FT the denominator from the candidate's value in (g).
